evidence: Cato Agr. 108: sī subacidum erit, nōn dūrābit
terms.comment: Cato’s word for a wine with a sour edge; of a pleasantly sharp taste, as of lemon, it is the softer word beside acidus.

phrases.english: It’s sour! Add a little honey.

phrases.latin: quod petis, id sānē est invīsum acidumque duōbus
phrases.english: what you ask for, the other two find hateful and sour

phrases.latin: Citreum subacidum est, sed mihi placet.
phrases.english: Lemon has a tart taste, but I like it.

phrases.latin: Sī id sapiet, quod in dōliō est, scītō dūrātūrum; sī subacidum erit, nōn dūrābit.
phrases.english: If it tastes like what is in the jar, you can be sure it will keep; if it is a little sour, it will not.

sources: Lewis & Short: acidus · Lewis & Short: subacidus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 280.
